- main:
  - generic: Transparency
  - heading "The rubric behind every score" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Cadence scores seven dimensions drawn from well-replicated research on effective instruction. Each is scored 1–4 with quoted evidence from the transcript. Weights reflect how reliably each can be judged from audio, not how much it matters.
  - article:
    - heading "Questioning depth" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Effective teachers ask many questions and a meaningful share probe reasoning (why/how/explain), not just recall.
    - generic: weight ×1.25
    - generic: "audio reliability: high"
    - generic: 1 · Emerging
    - generic: Few questions; almost all closed recall or rhetorical.
    - generic: 2 · Developing
    - generic: Regular questions but mostly closed; occasional 'why'.
    - generic: 3 · Secure
    - generic: Frequent questions with a clear share of open and reasoning questions.
    - generic: 4 · Exemplary
    - generic: Questions sequenced from recall to reasoning; students asked to justify, compare, evaluate.
    - generic: Rosenshine (2012) Principle 3
    - generic: Coe et al. (2020) Great Teaching Toolkit 4.1
    - generic: Bloom's taxonomy
  - article:
    - heading "Checking for understanding" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Checking all students (not just volunteers) lets the teacher adapt before misconceptions embed.
    - generic: weight ×1.25
    - generic: "audio reliability: high"
    - generic: 1 · Emerging
    - generic: No systematic checks; relies on 'any questions?' or volunteers.
    - generic: 2 · Developing
    - generic: Occasional checks, mostly hands-up or single students.
    - generic: 3 · Secure
    - generic: Regular whole-class checks (mini-whiteboards, cold call, hinge questions).
    - generic: 4 · Exemplary
    - generic: Frequent whole-class checks with visible adaptation based on responses.
    - generic: Rosenshine (2012) Principle 6
    - generic: "Lemov, Teach Like a Champion: Cold Call, Show Me"
    - generic: Wiliam (2011) Embedded Formative Assessment
  - article:
    - heading "Explanation & modelling" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Clear, small-step explanations with worked examples and explicit success criteria reduce cognitive load.
    - generic: weight ×1
    - generic: "audio reliability: high"
    - generic: 1 · Emerging
    - generic: Explanations unstructured; no worked example or success criteria.
    - generic: 2 · Developing
    - generic: Some structure; worked example or objective present but thin.
    - generic: 3 · Secure
    - generic: Clear objective, sequenced steps and at least one narrated worked example.
    - generic: 4 · Exemplary
    - generic: Expert thinking made visible; multiple examples/non-examples; steps explicitly signposted.
    - generic: Rosenshine (2012) Principles 2 & 4
    - generic: Sweller, Cognitive Load Theory
    - generic: Coe et al. (2020) GTT 3.1
  - article:
